stem: A Massachusetts sterile compounding applicant has held a provisional licence for eleven months. It has made real progress but will not reach full compliance for another two months, and asks the Board to extend the provisional licence for that period. What is the position?

choices.text: The Board may extend it once, for a period not exceeding six months.
The Board may extend it where the applicant shows continued substantial compliance.
The Board must extend it, since full compliance is the stated objective.
The Board may convert it now and inspect for full compliance afterwards.
The provisional licence may not be renewed or extended and lapses at one year.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 6.17 provides that a provisional licence is valid until the earliest of conversion, surrender, suspension or revocation, or ONE YEAR from issue, and states flatly that a provisional licence may not be renewed or extended. Conversion requires the Board to have determined the pharmacy is in FULL compliance, which has not happened here.

choice_analysis.A: No extension mechanism exists in the section.
choice_analysis.B: Substantial compliance is the entry test, not a ground for extension.
choice_analysis.C: Nothing obliges the Board to extend.
choice_analysis.D: Conversion follows a determination of full compliance, not precedes it.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: no renewal, no extension, one year outer limit.

related_facts: Substantial compliance plus potential to reach full compliance is the entry test
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates assume a regulator that grants a provisional status will also grant more time.

reasoning_steps: Identify the four events that end a provisional licence
Note the absence of any extension mechanism
